<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/modes/ -->

# Control modes

The driver is always in one control mode. A command that carries a setpoint switches to the mode that uses it;
`#Idle` or Send_Idle switches back to idle. The driver refuses the closed-loop modes while it is not calibrated or
while an error is active.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NotCalibrated: power-up, no saved calibration
    [*] --> Idle: power-up, saved calibration
    NotCalibrated --> Calibration: #Cal
    Calibration --> Idle: success, #Save
    Calibration --> NotCalibrated: a test fails
    Idle --> ControlMode: a setpoint
    ControlMode --> Idle: #Idle, Send_Idle
    ControlMode --> Error: a fault
    Idle --> Error: a fault
    Error --> Idle: #Clear, cause gone
```

A setpoint is `#P`, `#V`, `#Iq`, `#PD` or a CAN motion frame, and a new setpoint switches the mode without
passing through idle; a fault is any of the errors on [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/errors/).

| ControlMode | What the motor does | Entered by | Setpoint unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | nothing: coasts (phases open), or brakes (phases shorted) after `#Brake 1` or Send_Settings; with an error it always coasts, see [Braking in idle](#braking-in-idle) | `#Idle`, Send_Idle, `#Clear`, errors | — |
| Position | holds and moves to a position with the cascade of position, velocity and current loops | `#P`, Send_data_pack_1 (8 bytes) | encoder ticks |
| Velocity | turns at a speed with the velocity and current loops | `#V`, Send_data_pack_1 (5 bytes) | encoder ticks/s |
| Current (torque) | applies a current, so a torque, with the current loop alone | `#Iq`, Send_data_pack_1 (2 bytes) | mA |
| PD (impedance) | behaves like a spring and a damper around a position, with `KP` and `KD` | `#PD`, Send_data_pack_PD | encoder ticks |
| Voltage torque | applies a voltage on the q axis directly, without the current loop | `#Uq` | mV |
| Open loop | turns the stator field at a set electrical speed without the encoder in the loop; the rotor follows it like a stepper. It applies the voltage `#Openv` (5000 mV by default), not a current: `#Ilim` does not apply, and a low-resistance motor draws far more than its limit | `#Openloop` | electrical speed |
| Gripper | runs the gripper state machine: move to a jaw position with a speed and a current limit | `#Grippos`, Send_gripper_data_pack (with `#Gripper 1`) | 0 to 255 |
| Calibration | the calibration routine, or the gripper calibration | `#Cal`, `#Gripcal` | — |

## Braking in idle

`#Brake 1` (or Send_Settings over CAN) makes the idle motor brake: the driver keeps the three phases shorted, so
the motor resists being turned. `#Brake 0`, the default, lets it coast.

From firmware 110 `#Save` keeps the setting; on 109 every power-up started with coasting. Braking works only in idle
without an error; an error or an E-stop disables the driver, and the motor coasts.

!!! warning "The braking current is not limited"
    A motor that is turned while it brakes drives its own back-EMF current through the shorted phases, and the
    current loop does not limit that current. Use braking only on a motor whose resistance keeps the current under
    the driver's 2.8 A at the speeds it turns at.

## Units

- **Position** is in encoder ticks: 16384 per revolution of the motor shaft, counting up without limit over
  several revolutions. Positive is counter-clockwise seen from the encoder side of the board, see below.
- **Speed** is in encoder ticks per second: 16384 is one revolution per second, 60 rpm.
- **Current** is in mA. Torque is current times the motor's Kt, which calibration finds.
- **Feedforward**: the 8-byte motion frame carries a speed and a current feedforward beside the position, the
  5-byte one a current feedforward beside the speed. They are added after the loops, so a host that knows the
  trajectory can command it directly and leave the loops to correct the rest. Send 0 when you do not use them.

## Try it

<div class="calc" data-ticks-per-rev="16384" data-max-electrical-hz="500" markdown="0">
  <div class="calc__row calc__row--inline">
    <label for="uc-ticks">Ticks (a position, or a speed per second)</label>
    <input id="uc-ticks" type="number" name="ticks" step="1" value="16384">
    <label for="uc-pp">Pole pairs</label>
    <select id="uc-pp" name="pp">
      <option value="7">7</option>
      <option value="11" selected>11 (the gimbal motors)</option>
      <option value="14">14</option>
      <option value="21">21</option>
    </select>
  </div>
  <p class="calc__result">As a position: <strong data-out="turns">1.000</strong> turns, <strong data-out="deg">360.0°</strong> · as a speed: <strong data-out="rpm">60</strong> rpm · the practical maximum for <span data-out="ppout">11</span> pole pairs is about <strong data-out="maxrpm">2727</strong> rpm</p>
  <div class="calc__row calc__row--inline">
    <label for="uc-kt">Kt in Nm/A (what #Kt prints)</label>
    <input id="uc-kt" type="number" name="kt" step="0.01" min="0" value="0.30">
    <label for="uc-ma">Current in mA</label>
    <input id="uc-ma" type="number" name="ma" step="10" value="1000">
  </div>
  <p class="calc__result">Torque: <strong data-out="nm">0.30 Nm</strong>, <strong data-out="ncm">30 N·cm</strong></p>
</div>

The units of this page, with your numbers: 16384 encoder ticks per turn, the practical speed limit from the
electrical frequency the control loop can follow ([Ratings and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/03-technical-data/ratings/)), and
the torque as Kt times the current.

## Positive rotation

![Looking at the encoder side of the board, the side that faces the magnet, positive rotation is counter-clockwise. A positive current turns the motor that way, a positive speed too, and the position grows.](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/assets/Positive_rotation.webp){ width="520" }
![Looking at the encoder side of the board, the side that faces the magnet, positive rotation is counter-clockwise. A positive current turns the motor that way, a positive speed too, and the position grows.](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/assets/Positive_rotation_dark.webp){ width="520" }

The direction is tied to the encoder, not to the wiring: since firmware 105 calibration compensates the order of
the phases, so the motor turns the same way whichever wire went to which terminal.

## Which mode am I in?

`#Mode` prints the mode: `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`,
`Open loop`, `Gripper mode` or `Gripper calib mode`. In voltage-torque mode it prints nothing at all; `#Uq` then
prints the voltage setpoint.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/uart/ -->

# Over UART

The serial port is the interactive way to use the driver: you type a command, the driver answers in text. It is
the only way to calibrate, and the quickest way to try a setting. For real-time control of several motors use CAN.

## The protocol

A command is `#`, a name, optionally a space and one number, and a line ending:

```
#P 16384
#P
#Cal
```

- The name is case-sensitive and matches the firmware's spelling exactly (`#Kpiq`, not `#kpiq`); at most 19
  characters, the argument at most 19 characters and without spaces (`#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2`). Firmware 107 and
  older allowed 20 characters for both together.
- The line ends with LF (`\n`); a CR before it is accepted. Terminals send CR+LF when you press Enter, with the
  setting described in [The serial terminal](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/05-setup/terminal/).
- A **Set/Get** command with a number sets the value and prints it; without a number it only prints it. `#P 16384`
  moves to position 16384 and prints the position; `#P` prints the position. One exception: `#Openloop` without
  a number starts the motor at the stored open-loop speed.
- An **action** command takes no number: `#Cal`, `#Save`, `#Idle`.
- A name the driver does not know is answered with `Unknown command`; firmware 107 and older answered so also
  the few names its parser accepted but had no handler for.
- 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.

## The driver only answers

The driver never sends anything on its own, except with the cyclic commands: `#Cyc 100` makes it print position,
speed and Iq every 100 ms as `$ <position> <speed> <Iq>` (for BetterSerialPlotter), `#Cyca 100` as
`Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z` (for the Arduino plotter); `#Cyc` or `#Cyca` without a number stops it.

## Typical sessions

A first test after calibration:

```
#Ilim 1500        current limit for the motor
#V 16384          one revolution per second
#V 0
#P 0              back to the start
#Idle
```

Tuning:

```
#Kpv 0.02
#Kiv 0.001
#V 30000
#Save
```

Status:

```
#Info
#Error
#Temp
#Vbus
```

Every command is in the [UART reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/), grouped by what it does.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/can/ -->

# Over CAN

CAN is the interface for running a machine: compact frames, a fixed cost per message, up to 14 drivers on one bus,
and a host that can be a PC, a microcontroller or a robot control box.

The driver answers a motion command with its position, speed and current in the same frame exchange, so a control loop
on the host needs one frame out and one frame back per motor and cycle.

## The frame

CAN 2.0 data frames with 11-bit identifiers at 1 Mbit/s. The identifier carries the node, the command and the
error state:

![Bits 10 to 7 of the identifier are the node ID, bits 6 to 1 the command ID, bit 0 the error bit.](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/assets/can-id.svg){ width="600" }
![Bits 10 to 7 of the identifier are the node ID, bits 6 to 1 the command ID, bit 0 the error bit.](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/assets/can-id_dark.svg){ width="600" }

- **Node ID**, bits 10 to 7: which driver, 0 to 15. A driver acts only on frames with its own node ID and sends
  with it. Set it with `#CANID` or Send_CAN_ID and save; every driver ships as node 0. Use 0 to 13: the
  [bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/07-firmware/the-bootloader/) reserves 14 and 15, and a driver on one of those cannot be
  updated over CAN.
- **Command ID**, bits 6 to 1: which message, 0 to 63. The [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/) lists all of
  them.
- **Error bit**, bit 0: in a frame from the driver, 1 while any error is active. In a frame from the host it is
  ignored.

So a host sends Send_data_pack_1 (command 2) to node 3 with the identifier `(3 << 7) | (2 << 1)` = 0x184, and the
driver answers with command 3 under `(3 << 7) | (3 << 1) | error`. A lower node ID wins the bus arbitration.

Multi-byte values are big-endian: the most significant byte is in data[0] and goes first. Floats are IEEE 754
single precision. Flags inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit.

## Three kinds of message

- **Send_…**: the host sends data. Some of these are answered (a motion command with Respond_data_pack_1, the
  gripper command with Respond_Gripper_data_pack); most are not.
- **Send_Respond_…**: the host asks for data with a **remote frame** (the RTR bit set, no data) carrying the
  command ID; the driver answers with a data frame with the same command ID.
- **Respond_…**: frames only the driver sends: the answers above, and the heartbeat.

## A control loop

Send Send_data_pack_1 at a fixed rate, 100 Hz to 1 kHz, with the setpoint for this cycle; read Respond_data_pack_1
for the position, speed and current of the last cycle.

Every motion command (and every request the driver answers) resets the watchdog, so with Send_Watchdog set to a few
cycle times the motor stops when the host stops; from firmware 109 it can also hold its position, brake, coast or let
a joint down slowly ([The watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/watchdog/)).

Other frames, such as gains, limits, Send_Parameter or Send_Idle, do not reset it, and neither does anything sent over
UART. The heartbeat is the other way round: Send_Heartbeat_Setup makes the driver send a frame on its own every N ms
when it has nothing else to send, so the host can see it is alive.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Host
    participant D as Driver
    H->>D: Send_Clear_Error
    H->>D: Send_Watchdog: a few cycle times
    H->>D: Send_Heartbeat_Setup: every N ms
    loop every cycle, 100 Hz to 1 kHz
        H->>D: Send_data_pack_1: the setpoint, with the feedforwards
        D-->>H: Respond_data_pack_1: position, speed, current, the error bit
    end
    D-->>H: heartbeat, whenever nothing else was sent for N ms
    Note over D: no motion command within the watchdog time: watchdog error, the motor stops
```

## Parameters, identity and telemetry

From firmware 109 a host can also:

- set and read any setting by its number with Send_Parameter and Send_Get_Parameter (IDs 36 and 37, the answer on
  38), including the gains and limits in force, which it could not read back before
  ([Parameters and buffers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/parameters/));
- ask a drive what it is with Send_Respond_Identity (ID 39): product, tool, firmware release, pole pairs, whether
  it is calibrated;
- poll temperature, supply voltage, errors and current in one frame with Send_Respond_Telemetry (ID 40);
- record signals inside the control loop and read them with Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41)
  ([Status and diagnostics](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/diagnostics/)).

## From a PC

The [CANvas adapter](https://source-robotics.com/products/canvas-usb-to-can-adapter) shows up as a serial port and
speaks slcan; `python-can` opens it with `bustype='slcan'`. The Python library wraps the whole protocol, see
[With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/python/). Any CAN adapter that `python-can` supports works the same way.

## Several drivers

Give each driver its own node ID before you put them on one bus (a bus with two node 0s cannot tell them apart):
connect one driver at a time over UART, `#CANID 3`, `#Save`. Terminate the first and the last node, and wire the
daisy chain as in [Power and the CAN daisy chain](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/04-mounting/power-and-can/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/watchdog/ -->

# The watchdog

The watchdog stops the motor when the host stops talking: a host program that crashes, a cable that comes out,
a USB adapter that hangs. It is a timer in the driver.

Every valid motion frame and every request the driver answers starts it again; when it runs out, the driver raises the
watchdog error and does what its **action** says. From firmware 109 the action can hold the position, brake, coast, or
let a joint down slowly; before, the driver always disabled the motor, which then coasted.

## Setting it

=== "Python"
    ```python
    motor.Send_Watchdog(_rate=100, _action='Hold')   # 100 ms, then hold the position
    ```
    The library knows all five actions from 1.21: 'Idle', 'Hold', 'Brake', 'Coast' and 'Descend'. 1.20 and
    older know only 'Idle', 'Hold' and 'Brake'.

=== "CAN"
    Send_Watchdog (ID 15): the time in ms (4 bytes) and the action (1 byte). Or the parameters 6 (time) and 7
    (action) with Send_Parameter.

=== "Motor GUI"
    *Watchdog ms* in the settings.

0 ms switches it off, the default. Set it to a few of your host's cycle times: with a 100 Hz loop, 30 to 100 ms.
Send_Save_config keeps it, and a kept watchdog runs from power-up: a host that does not start sending within the
time finds the driver in watchdog error and clears it with Send_Clear_Error.

What starts the timer again: Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_gripper_data_pack, the
status requests (Send_Respond_…), Send_Get_Parameter and Send_Buffer_Read. Setting the watchdog time
(Send_Watchdog, parameter 6) starts a fresh window, and so does Send_Save_config, whose save takes time.

What does not: the other setting frames (gains, limits, Idle, Clear, Settings, Send_Parameter) and every UART command
(known issue KI-11). While the encoder table or the anti-cogging is measured, the driver feeds it itself.

## What a trip does

| Action | Name | What the driver does |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | legacy | what firmware 107 and older did: the motor driver is disabled and the motor coasts |
| 1 | hold | holds the position the motor had at the trip, for the fallback time; then the after-action |
| 2 | brake | shorts the phases at once; the braking current is not limited |
| 3 | coast | leaves the phases open at once: the motor turns freely |
| 4 | descend | applies the fallback current, but never lets the motor turn faster than the fallback speed, for the fallback time; then the after-action |

Any other action byte acts as 0. 0 is also what an unchanged host sends: the Python library's default, and what
the PAR6 runtime sends.

Three rules keep a gentler action from softening the response to a real fault:

- **Only a trip of the watchdog alone** gets the action. If another error is active as well (E-stop, encoder,
  supply voltage, temperature, not calibrated, a gripper E-stop), the driver gives the legacy response.
- **Hold and descend take over only from a running motor**: position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode. A
  driver that was idle when the watchdog ran out gives the legacy response: the motor coasts, also when it
  braked in idle (`#Brake 1`). From firmware 110 that holds also when a motion frame comes before the error is
  cleared; on 109 such a frame started the hold or the descend late, for the whole fallback time.
- **Hold and descend always end** after the fallback time, at most 60 s, so a lost host never leaves a motor
  driven for good. The after-action follows: 0 legacy, 2 brake or 3 coast.

The driver reports the watchdog error the whole time, and Send_Clear_Error (or `#Clear`) ends the action at
once and goes to idle; the next motion frame takes over.

### Hold

Hold keeps the position loop on the position the shaft had at the trip. Coming from position or velocity mode it
keeps the velocity integral too, so a joint under load does not sag at the moment of the trip.

A host that recovers within the fallback time (a USB hiccup) finds the joint where it left it. On the bench a gimbal
motor held within 6 ticks; with a load pulling on its shaft the holding current rose to 440 mA while the shaft crept
59 ticks.

### Descend

Descend applies the fallback current and limits the speed in both directions to the fallback speed. Inside the
cap the speed limiter's integral relaxes back to zero (within about 0.25 s), so it holds back only what keeps the
speed at the cap and never more:

- a joint under gravity with 0 mA lowers itself at no more than the cap speed and rests on whatever stops it;
- a gripper with its gripping current keeps its grip, and its jaws cannot slam shut;
- a free motor with a current turns at about the cap speed: on the bench a gimbal motor with 200 mA and a 1000
  ticks/s cap turned at 1145 to 1163 ticks/s, about 15 % over the cap, which is soft because the limiter's
  integral relaxes inside it.

It starts with the velocity integral at zero, so gravity can take the joint down.

## The fallback

Four values, kept by Send_Save_config in settings block 2:

| Parameter | `#WdFb` position | What | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1st | how long hold or descend runs, ms (0 to 60000) | 2000 |
| 3 | 2nd | the current descend applies, mA (signed) | 0 |
| 4 | 3rd | the speed cap of descend, ticks/s (0 to 65535) | 1000 |
| 5 | 4th | the after-action: 0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast | 0 |

=== "Terminal"
    ```
    #WdFb 2000,0,1000,2
    #Save
    ```
    Four numbers, commas, no spaces. `#WdFb` alone prints them, and `#Info` prints the watchdog with them.

=== "Python"
    ```python
    motor.Send_Watchdog_Fallback(2000, current_mA=0, speed=1000, after='Brake')
    motor.Send_Save_config()
    ```
    Library 1.21 and newer.

## Choosing an action

- **A bare motor on the bench, a conveyor, a wheel**: brake (2) stops it fastest; coast (3) or legacy (0) lets it
  run out.
- **A joint that carries a load**: hold (1) for a second or two, so a short loss of the host does not move it,
  then descend (4) with 0 mA for a joint that gravity pulls down, or brake for one it does not. Choose the cap
  speed for a joint you can still catch by hand.
- **A gripper**: descend with the gripping current, its sign the closing direction, keeps an object held.

These suggestions are untested on an assembled robot arm; try the action on your machine before you rely on it.
Brake is not current-limited (known issue KI-12): a load that drives a braking motor fast drives a large current
through the phases; try it with the motor still first.

## Seeing a trip

A capture armed with the error trigger (parameter 28 = 2) records the moments before and after a trip, the
watchdog's included: [Status and diagnostics](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/diagnostics/#a-capture).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/python/ -->

# With Python

The `Spectral-BLDC` library wraps the CAN protocol: one method per message, and the driver's answers unpacked into
attributes. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS with any adapter `python-can` supports, such as the CANvas adapter
over slcan.

## Installing

In a virtual environment:

=== "Windows"
    ```
    py -m venv .venv
    .venv\Scripts\activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `COM` and a number (Device Manager, **Ports (COM & LPT)**): `channel='COM41'`.

=== "Linux"
    ```
    python3 -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER     # access to the serial port; log out and in again once
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `/dev/ttyACM0` (`ls /dev/ttyACM*` lists it): `channel='/dev/ttyACM0'`.

=== "macOS"
    ```
    python3 -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `/dev/cu.usbmodem` and a number (`ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*` lists it):
    `channel='/dev/cu.usbmodem1101'`, with your number.

!!! success "Check"
    `python -c "import Spectral_BLDC"` returns without an error message.

The source and the examples are in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python).
For joints with a gear ratio and an offset, the [Source Robotics Toolbox](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Source-Robotics-Toolbox)
(`pip install SourceRoboticsToolbox`) turns encoder ticks into joint angles.

## The first program

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import time

# the adapter: a CANvas on COM41 (Windows) or /dev/ttyACM0 (Linux), 1 Mbit/s
comms = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM41', bitrate=1000000)
# the driver with node ID 0
motor = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=comms)

motor.Send_Clear_Error()

# A configured, calibrated motor with a clear shaft: command one turn for five seconds.
# Each command requests a fresh position/speed/current reply; heartbeat is not required.
try:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5.0
    next_cycle = time.monotonic()
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        motor.Send_data_pack_1(Position=16384, Speed=0, Current=0)
        reply_deadline = min(deadline, time.monotonic() + 0.02)
        while time.monotonic() < reply_deadline:
            message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(
                timeout=max(0.0, reply_deadline - time.monotonic()))
            if message is None:
                print("No motion feedback in this cycle; check the bus and node ID")
                break
            if ids.node_id != 0 or ids.command_id != 3:  # Respond_data_pack_1
                continue
            motor.UnpackData(message, ids)
            print(motor.position, motor.speed, motor.current, ids.error_bit)
            if ids.error_bit:
                raise RuntimeError("Driver fault: inspect State_of_Errors before retrying")
            break
        next_cycle += 0.02
        time.sleep(max(0.0, next_cycle - time.monotonic()))
finally:
    motor.Send_Idle()                    # also on Ctrl-C; the shaft no longer holds torque
```

`receive_can_messages` returns the raw `python-can` message and a tuple with the node ID, the command ID and the
error bit of the identifier; `UnpackData` decodes the message into the attributes the message carries.

This example resends the same setpoint at 50 Hz for five seconds, prints only matching motion feedback, and puts the
motor in idle when it ends. Idle releases torque: support any attached mechanism before running it. A missing reply is
reported without claiming that a move finished. Configure and calibrate the driver first
([Quick start](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/quick-start/)).

!!! success "Check"
    The program prints a line of position, speed, current and error bit for each cycle, the position moves to
    16384 and the error bit stays 0. `No motion feedback in this cycle` means no answer came back: the port, the
    node ID and the bus, see [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/can/).

## What is where

| Library call | Message | What you get back |
|---|---|---|
| `Send_data_pack_1(Position, Speed, Current)` | Send_data_pack_1 | `position`, `speed`, `current` |
| `Send_data_pack_PD(...)` | Send_data_pack_PD | `position`, `speed`, `current` |
| `Send_Respond_Encoder_data()` | Send_Respond_Encoder_data | `position`, `speed` (32-bit) |
| `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()` | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors | the error attributes |
| `Send_gripper_data_pack(...)` | Send_gripper_data_pack | `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, the gripper state bits |
| `Send_Limits(...)`, `Send_Velocity_Gains(...)`, ... | the setting messages | nothing; `Send_Save_config()` keeps them |

The complete map of calls to messages is in the [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/python/) reference, and each
message's bytes in the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/).

## Several motors

One `CanCommunication` per bus, one `SpectralCAN` per driver with its node ID. Send to each, then read the bus:
every answer carries the node ID in `ids.node_id`, so route it to the right object.

```python
motors = [Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=i, communication=comms) for i in range(3)]
for m in motors:
    m.Send_Respond_Encoder_data()
for _ in motors:
    message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.1)
    if message is not None:
        motors[ids.node_id].UnpackData(message, ids)
```

The [Guides](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/guides/) build on this: a quadruped leg, gravity compensation, bilateral teleoperation.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/motor-gui/ -->

# Working in Motor GUI

Everyday use of the driver from [Motor GUI](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/05-setup/motor-gui/): moving the motor, watching it, recording
what it does, running several motors, and the few things that only work from the console.

## Moving the motor

The jog controls send setpoints in the matching control mode: *Jog velocity* turns the motor at a speed in encoder
ticks per second (16384 is one revolution per second), *Jog position* moves it to a position in ticks, *Jog
current* applies a torque in mA.

*Send setpoint* sends a value in the mode the driver is in. Idle stops the motor; [Control modes](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/modes/) says what
each mode does. With *Live stream while dragging* the setpoint follows the slider, which is the quickest way to feel a
tuning change.

## Watching it

The plots show position, speed and current as the driver reports them. Pan and zoom to a move; hover for the
value. A step in the position setpoint shows overshoot and settling at once, a speed step shows the velocity
loop's response; [Current limit and loop tuning](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/05-setup/tuning/) uses them step by step.

## Recording

A recording keeps the telemetry stream to a file: *New recording*, run the move, *Stop recording*. Record the
response before and after a tuning change to compare them, or a failure to attach to a bug report
([Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/support/report-a-problem/)).

## Clearing errors

The errors the driver reports are listed with the state; **Clear errors** sends what `#Clear` does. An error whose
cause is still present comes straight back; [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/errors/) says what each one needs.

## Several motors

Over the CANvas adapter the GUI sees every driver on the bus and addresses each by its node ID.

Give each driver its own ID over the serial adapter first (the CAN node ID in the settings, then Save), terminate the
first and the last node, and set a watchdog (*Watchdog ms*) on a bus that drives something that must not run away:
[Power and the CAN daisy chain](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/04-mounting/power-and-can/), [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/can/).

## Gripper

A driver in gripper mode shows the gripper controls: calibrate the jaws, a position from open to closed, a speed,
a current limit, and the state the gripper reports. *No gripper connection* means the driver is not in gripper
mode or not on the bus. [Gripper mode](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/gripper-mode/).

## Firmware updates

*Firmware update* lists the releases from GitHub and flashes one through the bootloader; on a bus, *Scan
bootloaders* finds the boards. [Updating through the bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/07-firmware/update/).

## The console

Anything the GUI has no control for is one `#` command away in the console, with the driver's answer below it;
the whole set is in the [UART commands](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/) reference. The cyclic output (`#Cyc`) is what
the GUI's telemetry stream uses over serial, so do not start it by hand while the plots run.

## Reading a fault

<figure class="gui-shot" markdown="1">
<div class="gui-shot__image" markdown="1">

<span class="gui-shot__mark" style="left:1%;top:14%" aria-hidden="true">1</span>
<span class="gui-shot__mark" style="left:7%;top:57%" aria-hidden="true">2</span>
<span class="gui-shot__mark" style="left:13%;top:81%" aria-hidden="true">3</span>

</div>
<figcaption markdown="1">**1. Errors state:** a fault is active. **2. Errors tab:** inspect individual flags. **3. E-stop error:** 1 identifies the latched fault in this simulation. **4. Clear errors:** clear it after removing its cause; a persistent cause returns on the next update. Screenshot captured from **Mock CAN (demo)**.</figcaption>
</figure>

!!! success "Check"
    After recovery the fault flag returns to 0 and the state shows *No errors*. If it returns, stop and follow
    [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/errors/).
