# Gains and limits

The commands that set the loop gains and the limits. None of them is answered; save with Send_Save_config.

### Send_PD_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 16</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_PD_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets KP and KD, the gains of the impedance (PD) loop. Keep them with Send_Save_config.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | KP | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 | KD | float 32 |  |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Current_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 17</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Current_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI current loop of Iq. The Id loop keeps its gains; over UART, `#Kpiq` and `#Kiiq` set both loops, and so do parameters 11 and 12.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Kp_iq | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 | Ki_iq | float 32 |  |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Velocity_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 18</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Velocity_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI velocity loop.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Kpv | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 | Kiv | float 32 |  |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Position_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 19</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Position_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp of the P position loop.

**4 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Kpp | float 32 |  |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Limits

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 20</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Limits()`</span></div>

Sets the speed limit and the current limit the loops may reach. From firmware 109 a negative value, or one that is not a number, is ignored, and the current limit stops at the driver's 2800 mA, as with `#Ilim`. Firmware 107 and older stored the current limit as it arrived. Never send more than the motor's rating.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Speed limit | float 32 | encoder ticks/s |
| 4-7 | Current limit | float 32 | mA |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Kt

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 22</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Kt()`</span></div>

Sets the motor's torque constant Kt, which the driver uses to estimate torque from current.

**4 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Kt | float 32 | Nm/A |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Voltage_Limit

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 34</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Voltage_Limit()`</span></div>

Sets the voltage limit of the current loops (the same value as `#Vlim`), in mV. 0 means use the supply voltage. In the 104 release image (the source at tag V104 does not have it yet) and in every release from 105. From firmware 109 it takes 0 to 60000 mV, as parameter 17 does; a value outside is ignored.

**4 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Voltage limit | signed 32-bit | mV; 0 = Vbus |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/status/ -->

# Status requests

Data the host asks for with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data); the driver answers with a data frame with the same command ID. And the heartbeat, which the driver sends on its own.

### Send_Respond_Ping

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 10</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Ping()`</span></div>

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

**The frame** (0 bytes) carries no data.

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Ping**.

---

### Send_Respond_Temperature

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 23</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Temperature()`</span></div>

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

**The frame** (2 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Temperature**.

---

### Send_Respond_Voltage

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 24</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Voltage()`</span></div>

Asks for the supply voltage.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | voltage | unsigned 16-bit | mV |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Voltage**.

---

### Send_Respond_Device_Info

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 25</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Device_Info()`</span></div>

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

**The frame** (7 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | HARDWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision |
| 1 | BATCH_DATE | unsigned 8-bit | production batch, the lowest 8 bits of the stored value (24092024 after #Default is sent as 120) |
| 2 | SOFTWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | firmware release, e.g. 107 |
| 3-6 | SERIAL_NUMBER | unsigned 32-bit | serial number |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Device_Info**.

---

### Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 26</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()`</span></div>

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated, watchdog and product-lock states.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | error | bit | any error is active |
| 0 | 6 | temperature_error | bit | motor over the temperature limit |
| 0 | 5 | encoder_error | bit | magnet not detected or misaligned |
| 0 | 4 | vbus_error | bit | supply voltage outside the limits |
| 0 | 3 | driver_error | bit | the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent |
| 0 | 2 | velocity_error | bit | speed over the limit |
| 0 | 1 | current_error | bit | reserved; never set by this firmware |
| 0 | 0 | estop_error | bit | Send_ESTOP was received (from firmware 110 also #Estop over UART) |
| 1 | 7 | calibrated | bit | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | 6 | activated | bit | the controller is activated |
| 1 | 5 | watchdog_error | bit | the watchdog ran out |
| 1 | 4 | wrong_product | bit | from firmware 109: this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors**.

---

### Send_Respond_Iq_data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 27</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Iq_data()`</span></div>

Asks for the measured Iq current.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | current | signed 16-bit | mA |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Iq_data**.

---

### Send_Respond_Encoder_data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 28</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Encoder_data()`</span></div>

Asks for the position and the filtered speed, as 32-bit values. Python attributes `position` and `speed`.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | position | signed 32-bit | encoder ticks |
| 4-7 | speed | signed 32-bit | encoder ticks/s |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Encoder_data**.

---

### Send_Respond_Kt

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 33</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Kt()`</span></div>

Asks for the torque constant Kt the driver uses. Added in firmware 104.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Kt | float 32 | Nm/A |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Kt**.

---

### Send_Respond_Identity

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 39</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Identity()`</span></div>

Asks what the drive is: the product, the tool it is built into, the firmware release, the hardware version, the pole pairs, whether it is calibrated, and eight flags. A host can check it before it commands or flashes a drive. Added in firmware 109. Python attributes `product_id`, `product_name`, `tool_id`, `firmware_version`, `identity_hardware_version`, `pole_pairs`, `identity_calibrated`, `identity_flags`.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | product | unsigned 8-bit | 1 STEPFOC, 2 Spectral Micro: the firmware that answers |
| 1 |  | tool_id | unsigned 8-bit | parameter 1: 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own |
| 2-3 |  | firmware_version | unsigned 16-bit | the release, e.g. 109 |
| 4 |  | hardware_version | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision from the EEPROM |
| 5 |  | pole_pairs | unsigned 8-bit | the motor's pole pairs; 0 if outside 0-255 |
| 6 |  | calibrated | unsigned 8-bit | 1 calibrated, 0 not |
| 7 | 0 | gripper | bit | the driver is set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1) |
| 7 | 1 | brake_on_idle | bit | idle brakes (1) or coasts (0) |
| 7 | 2 | commutation_reversed | bit | calibration found the coils wired the other way round |
| 7 | 3 | settings_block2 | bit | the EEPROM has the bank settings block 2 lives in, so parameters 1-5 can be saved |
| 7 | 4 | wrong_product | bit | this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing |
| 7 | 5 | sense_zero_measured | bit | the current-sense zero was measured at start-up and is plausible |
| 7 | 6 | cogging_saved | bit | the anti-cogging in use is the one saved in the EEPROM |
| 7 | 7 | switching_zero_in_use | bit | the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46) |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Identity**.

The flags in byte 7 are numbered the usual way, bit 0 the least significant (unlike the error bytes, which the firmware packs from bit 7 down).

---

### Send_Respond_Telemetry

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 40</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Telemetry()`</span></div>

Asks for the temperature, the supply voltage, both error bytes and the current in one frame, all from the same moment: one request instead of four. Added in firmware 109. The Python library fills the same attributes as the four separate answers.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C (meaningful with the thermistor enabled) |
| 2-3 | voltage | signed 16-bit | supply voltage in mV |
| 4 | errors_1 | unsigned 8-bit | the error flags, as byte 0 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors |
| 5 | errors_2 | unsigned 8-bit | calibrated, activated, watchdog, wrong product, as byte 1 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors |
| 6-7 | current | signed 16-bit | Iq in mA |

</div>

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Telemetry**.

---

### Respond_Heartbeat

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 9</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

**The frame** (0 bytes) carries no data.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). The driver answers to the new ID at once. The ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config, and saving is also what copies it into the bootloader's board ID.

**1 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 13 (14 and 15 are accepted but reserved by the bootloader) |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode: the motor coasts, or brakes when Send_Settings or `#Brake 1` asked for it.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM, and copies the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. From firmware 109 it also writes the tool id and the watchdog fallback (settings block 2), the anti-cogging set with its mode and scale, and the encoder table with its on/off flag, parameter 56 and the current-sense zero trims, each block with its own checksum; of the two large blocks only the 16-byte pages that changed are written. From firmware 110 it also writes the idle behaviour of Send_Settings (parameter 18). Not kept: the current loop bandwidth, and every parameter the parameter table marks as not kept. A drive stopped by the product lock writes nothing.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 104 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle; it also ends a watchdog hold or descend. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog. The motion commands (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_gripper_data_pack) and the requests the driver answers (the Send_Respond_ remote frames, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Buffer_Read) reset it; the other frames (Send_Parameter among them) and UART commands do not. When the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. 0 turns it off (the default). From firmware 109 the driver acts on the action byte, but only when the watchdog is the only active error: any other error gets the legacy response, the motor disabled and coasting. Hold and descend run for the fallback time (parameter 2, 2 s by default), then the after-action (parameter 5); they start only if the driver was in position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode, otherwise the driver gives the legacy response and the motor coasts. Setting the time starts a fresh window, and a negative time means off. [The watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/watchdog/) explains each action. The setting is kept by Send_Save_config. The same values are parameters 6 and 7, which `#Par` reaches over UART: to turn off a saved watchdog, send 0 over CAN or `#Par 6,0`, and save.

**5 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 legacy (the motor disabled, coasting), 1 hold the position, 2 brake (not current-limited), 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0 |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

Firmware 107 and older store the action byte without acting on it. The Python library sends all five actions from 1.21 ('Idle', 'Hold', 'Brake', 'Coast', 'Descend'); 1.20 and older send only 0, 1 or 2.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

</div>

---

### Send_Settings

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 35</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">2 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Settings()`</span></div>

Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast (the default). From firmware 110 Send_Save_config keeps it; on 109 the driver coasted again after a power cycle, as a driver still does that never saved it. Braking applies only in idle without an error; an error always disables the motor, which then coasts. The braking current is not limited, see Control modes. Added in firmware 107 (STEPFOC 107). The Python library has `Send_Settings(mask, value)` and, for this bit, `Send_Brake_Coast(brake)` from 1.21; 1.20 and older have no call for it.

**2 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Mask | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0 = write the idle behaviour |
| 1 | Value | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0: 1 brake, 0 coast |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Cyclic_command

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 29</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">not implemented</span></div>

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/parameters/ -->

# Parameters and buffers

From firmware 109 a setting that has no command of its own is a **parameter**: a number from 1 to 93 (89 in firmware
109) behind one pair of commands, Send_Parameter (ID 36) to set it and Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) to read it,
answered with Respond_Parameter (ID 38). The identifier has room for only 64 command IDs, so new settings no longer
use them up.

Parameter numbers are permanent: a number is never given a new meaning. Number 73 is not used and stays free.
Parameters 84 to 87 are read only and say which build and which board answer: the git commit the firmware was built
from (84), its build time in Unix seconds (85), the board ID (86) and the calibration ID (87). `#Info` prints them
as `Build`, `Board ID` and `Calibration ID` ([Status and diagnostics](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/diagnostics/)).
Parameters 88 and 89, a diagnostic of when the current sensors are read, are the Spectral Micro's own; STEPFOC does
not have them.

Firmware 110 adds 90 to 93: the three settings that only UART could set before, `#Rstint` (90), `#Term`, the
thermistor (91) and `#Gripper`, gripper mode (92), and the gripper's stroke (93, read only). The Spectral-BLDC
library 1.22 names them (`PARAM_RSTINT`, `PARAM_THERMISTOR`, `PARAM_GRIPPER_MODE`, `PARAM_GRIPPER_STROKE`); 1.21
sets and reads them by their numbers.

The **buffers** are the larger data a drive holds: a capture of three signals, a histogram, the anti-cogging set
and the encoder table. Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41) reads them in 8-byte frames, Respond_Buffer_Data (ID 42) carries
them, and Send_Buffer_Write (ID 43) writes the anti-cogging set.

Over UART, `#Par` does the same: `#Par` lists every parameter, `#Par 1` reads one, `#Par 1,200` sets it
([Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/utility/)).

## Setting and reading a parameter

A set is not answered: read the value back to know what the driver took. A value outside a parameter's range is
clamped, replaced or refused, as the table says, and a read-only number ignores the write.

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral

comms = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM41', bitrate=1000000)
motor = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=comms)

motor.Send_Parameter(1, 200)               # tool id 200, a custom tool
motor.Send_Get_Parameter(1)                # read it back
message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.1)
if message is not None:
    motor.UnpackData(message, ids)
print(motor.parameters.get(1))
motor.Send_Save_config()                   # keep it over a power cycle
```

`Send_Parameter`, `Send_Get_Parameter` and the buffer calls need the Spectral-BLDC library 1.21 or newer.
`Send_Parameter` takes the value itself: a gain or a limit (8 to 16 and 20) is sent as a float, so
`motor.Send_Parameter(16, 1500)` sets a current limit of 1500 mA; every other parameter takes a whole number.

## The commands

### Send_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 36</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Parameter()`</span></div>

Sets one parameter by its number (the [parameter table](#every-parameter)). Firmware 109 gives new settings a parameter number instead of a command ID of their own, since the identifier has room for only 64 command IDs. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused as the table says; a number the firmware does not know, or a read-only one, is ignored. The driver does not answer: read the value back with Send_Get_Parameter. A value set this way lives in RAM until Send_Save_config, like every other setting; the table says which parameters Save keeps.

**5 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number, 1-93 |
| 1-4 | Value | signed 32-bit | the new value, in the parameter's unit; for the gains, limits and Kt (8-16, 20) a float's bit pattern |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

A data frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored and flagged as a wrong data length. It does not reset the watchdog.

---

### Send_Get_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 37</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Get_Parameter()`</span></div>

Asks for the value in force of one parameter. The answer, Respond_Parameter, comes under ID 38, not 37: a host and a driver must never send data frames with the same identifier, because two sent at the same moment collide. Resets the watchdog. The Python library stores the value in `parameters[number]`.

**1 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number |

</div>

The driver answers with **Respond_Parameter**.

---

### Respond_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 38</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span></div>

The answer to Send_Get_Parameter: the number and the value in force. For a number the firmware does not know the frame carries the number alone (1 byte; the Python library sets `unknown_parameter`). The gains, limits and Kt (parameters 8 to 16 and 20) travel as the bit pattern of an IEEE-754 float, the others as integers.

**The frame** (5 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number |
| 1-4 | value | signed 32-bit | the value in force; a float's bits for 8-16 and 20 |

</div>

---

### Send_Buffer_Read

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 41</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Buffer_Read()`</span></div>

Asks for entries of one of the drive's buffers: the capture, the histogram, the anti-cogging harmonics or table, or the encoder table. The driver answers with one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per entry (for the two tables, one per three values), sent from its main loop whenever a transmit mailbox is free, so a long read-out never holds up the control loop or other answers. A new request replaces one still in progress; count 0 cancels it. Entries past the end are not sent. Resets the watchdog.

**5 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Kind | unsigned 8-bit | 0 capture (up to 1024 samples: parameter 32 says how many), 1 histogram (256 bins), 2 anti-cogging harmonics (8 slots), 3 anti-cogging table (256 values), 4 encoder table (128 values) |
| 1-2 | First | unsigned 16-bit | the first index |
| 3-4 | Count | unsigned 16-bit | how many entries; 0 cancels a read-out |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Respond_Buffer_Data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 42</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span></div>

One entry of a buffer, the answer to Send_Buffer_Read. The first two bytes say which: the kind in the top three bits, the index in the other thirteen (kind × 8192 + index). The six bytes after them depend on the kind, as the table below the frame says.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | header | unsigned 16-bit | kind × 8192 + index |
| 2-3 | word_a | signed 16-bit | capture: channel A; histogram: the count (unsigned); harmonics: the harmonic number (0 = slot unused); tables: entry index |
| 4-5 | word_b | signed 16-bit | capture: channel B; histogram: the sum's upper 16 bits; harmonics: a, the cosine term in mA; tables: entry index + 1 |
| 6-7 | word_c | signed 16-bit | capture: channel C; histogram: the sum's lower 16 bits; harmonics: b, the sine term in mA; tables: entry index + 2 (0 past the end) |

</div>

| Kind | Index | Bytes 2-7 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 capture | the sample, oldest first, 0 to parameter 32 − 1 | channels A, B and C, each in its signal's unit (the parameter table lists the signals) |
| 1 histogram | the bin, 0-255 over one electrical turn or one motor turn | the count (unsigned 16-bit), then the sum (signed 32-bit); the bin's mean is sum ÷ count |
| 2 anti-cogging harmonics | the slot, 0-7 | the harmonic of the electrical angle (1-32, 0 = unused), a and b in mA: the slot adds a·cos(h·θ) + b·sin(h·θ) |
| 3 anti-cogging table | the first of three values, 0-255 | three values in mA, 64 angle counts apart (256 per electrical turn) |
| 4 encoder table | the first of three values, 0-127 | three corrections in 1/16 encoder count, 128 per motor turn |

---

### Send_Buffer_Write

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 43</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Cogging_Harmonic(), Send_Cogging_Table()`</span></div>

Writes the anti-cogging set: kind 2 one harmonic slot per frame, kind 3 three table values per frame, in the Respond_Buffer_Data layout. Other kinds are ignored (the encoder table cannot be written), and so is a harmonic above 32. The set lives in RAM until Send_Save_config; switch it on with parameter 37. The driver does not answer.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | Header | unsigned 16-bit | kind × 8192 + index; kind 2 or 3 |
| 2-3 | Word A | signed 16-bit | kind 2: the harmonic (1-32, 0 = unused); kind 3: value at index |
| 4-5 | Word B | signed 16-bit | kind 2: a in mA; kind 3: value at index + 1 |
| 6-7 | Word C | signed 16-bit | kind 2: b in mA; kind 3: value at index + 2 |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---

## Every parameter

The number and the name are read from the firmware; the rest is checked against its source. *Access*: a read-only
parameter ignores a write; a run parameter starts or stops a run when written and gives its state when read.

### Watchdog and tool

Parameters 1 to 5 live in settings block 2 of the EEPROM, 6 and 7 in the first settings block beside the other settings; Send_Save_config keeps all seven. A value outside a range is clamped, replaced or ignored, as the Value column says.

<div class="ref-table params" markdown>

| No. | What it is | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What the drive is built into. For an MSG the tens digit is the rail (1 = 100, 2 = 150, 3 = 200 mm) and the units digit the stepper (1 = 21.5, 2 = 40, 3 = 60 mm). Also `#Tool`; reported in the identity frame.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_TOOL_ID` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2</span> | 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own tools; a value outside 0-255 is ignored. Default 0 |
| 2 | How long watchdog hold or descend runs before the after-action takes over.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_TIME` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2</span> | ms, 0-60000 (clamped). Default 2000 |
| 3 | The current watchdog descend applies. 0 lets gravity lower a joint; a gripper gets its grip current.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_CURRENT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2</span> | mA, signed, -32768 to 32767 (outside: 0). Default 0 |
| 4 | The speed watchdog descend never exceeds, in either direction.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_SPEED` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2</span> | ticks/s, 0-65535 (outside: 1000). Default 1000 |
| 5 | What follows hold or descend when the fallback time has run out.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_AFTER_ACTION` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2</span> | 0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast (any other value: 0). Default 0 |
| 6 | The watchdog time, the same value Send_Watchdog sets.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_TIME` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 1</span> | ms, 0 = off (a negative value: 0). Default 0 |
| 7 | What a trip of the watchdog alone does, the same value as byte 4 of Send_Watchdog.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_WD_ACTION` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 1</span> | 0 legacy, 1 hold, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend (outside 0-255: 0; 5-255 act as legacy). Default 0 |

</div>

### Gains, limits and settings

The values in force, readable and writable by parameter (their own commands, given in each row, still work). A float travels as its IEEE-754 bit pattern, big-endian, the way the gain commands send it; over UART `#Par 9,0.02` sets Kpv. A write goes to RAM like the commands' own; Send_Save_config keeps it. Parameter 23, the product stamp, stays read only.

<div class="ref-table params" markdown>

| No. | What it is | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Kp of the position loop (Send_Position_Gains, `#Kpp`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KPP` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 9 | Kp of the velocity loop (Send_Velocity_Gains, `#Kpv`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KPV` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 10 | Ki of the velocity loop (Send_Velocity_Gains, `#Kiv`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KIV` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 11 | Kp of the current loops; writing it sets the Iq and the Id loop, as `#Kpiq` does (Send_Current_Gains sets the Iq loop only). A calibration and parameter 49 set it too.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KPIQ` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 12 | Ki of the current loops; writing it sets the Iq and the Id loop, as `#Kiiq` does (Send_Current_Gains sets the Iq loop only). A calibration and parameter 49 set it too.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KIIQ` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 13 | KP, the stiffness of the impedance (PD) loop (Send_PD_Gains).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KP` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 14 | KD, the damping of the impedance (PD) loop (Send_PD_Gains).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KD` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) |
| 15 | The velocity limit (Send_Limits, `#Vlimit`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_VELOCITY_LIMIT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float, ticks/s; 0 or more, below 10^9 (otherwise refused) |
| 16 | The current limit (Send_Limits, `#Ilim`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CURRENT_LIMIT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float, mA; 0-2800 (negative or above 2800: refused) |
| 17 | The voltage limit of the current loops (Send_Voltage_Limit, `#Vlim`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_VOLTAGE_LIMIT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | mV, 0-60000 (outside: refused); 0 = the supply voltage |
| 18 | The idle behaviour (Send_Settings bit 0, `#Brake`).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_BRAKE_COAST` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes, settings block 2, from firmware 110 (109 coasted at every power-up). Never saved, and after `#Default`: coast</span> | 1 brake, 0 coast (any value but 0: brake) |
| 19 | The heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_HEARTBEAT_MS` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | ms, 0-60000 (outside: refused); 0 = off |
| 20 | The torque constant (Send_Kt, `#Kt`, calibration).<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_KT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | float, Nm/A; 0 or more, below 10^9 (otherwise refused) |
| 23 | The product lock: the product that calibrated this board. Stamped at the first start-up of a calibrated board and at every save. | 90 | Whether the velocity and current integrators are reset on every new setpoint command (`#Rstint`). Added in firmware 110.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_RSTINT` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | 0 or 1 (anything else: refused). Default 0 |
| 91 | The thermistor measurement and the temperature error (`#Term`). Added in firmware 110.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_THERMISTOR` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: yes</span> | 0 off, 1 on (anything else: refused). Default 0 |
| 92 | Gripper mode (`#Gripper`), in force at once: the driver then reads its commands as a gripper, or as a motor. It is written only while the driver is idle, so a move is never cut over half-way. ### Current sensing and the current loop

The current-sense zero is the ADC reading with no current flowing, in counts from 2048 (1 count is about 1.6 mA). The driver measures it at every start-up with the bridge off; the trim is added to it.

<div class="ref-table params" markdown>

| No. | What it is | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | The current-sense zero of channel 1 in use. | 22 | The current-sense zero of channel 2 in use, as 21.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no: measured again at every start-up</span> | counts from 2048, -400 to 400 (outside: refused) |
| 40 | The zero of channel 1 measured with the bridge off, the trim added.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET_OFF` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no: measured at every start-up</span> | counts from 2048 |
| 41 | The zero of channel 2 measured with the bridge off, the trim added.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET_OFF` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no: measured at every start-up</span> | counts from 2048 |
| 42 | The second zero measurement, made in idle after start-up with the bridge switching at 50 % duty. On the bench it made the current ripple worse, so it is measured and kept but not used unless 46 asks for it.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_SENSE_ZERO_SWITCHING` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no</span> | 0 not run, 1 measuring, 2 in use, 3 rejected (implausible), 4 interrupted (a command or an error came first), 5 measured, not in use |

### Capture and histogram

The signal numbers: 0 none, 1 measured Iq (mA), 2 measured Id (mA), 3 Iq setpoint with the anti-cogging (mA), 4 speed (ticks/s, saturates at ±32767), 5 speed ÷ 16, 6 position (ticks, the low 16 bits), 7 position error (ticks), 8 electrical angle (0-16383 per electrical turn, from the encoder alone), 9 encoder (0-16383 per motor turn), 10 Vbus (10 mV), 11 and 12 the two current-sense readings (counts after the zero), 13 the control interrupt's time (µs), 14 the anti-cogging feedforward (mA), 15 the Iq setpoint without the anti-cogging (mA), 16 the Uq setpoint (mV), 17 and 18 the d and q voltage the output transform received (mV). None of these settings is saved.

<div class="ref-table params" markdown>

| No. | What it is | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 24 | The signal of channel A, which is also the trigger channel.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_A` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 4, speed |
| 25 | The signal of channel B.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_B` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 1, Iq |
| 26 | The signal of channel C.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_C` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 8, electrical angle |
| 27 | One sample every N control loops of 200 µs.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_DIVIDER` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | control loops per sample, 1-65535 (clamped). Default 1 |
| 28 | 1 to 4 clear the buffer and arm a capture; 0 stops one and keeps what was recorded. The error trigger fires when the error flag rises, a watchdog trip included; an error already present does not fire it.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_TRIGGER` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | 0 stop, 1 now, 2 on an error, 3 channel A rising through the level, 4 falling through it (outside: 0) |
| 29 | The level of triggers 3 and 4.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_LEVEL` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | channel A's unit, -32768 to 32767 (saturated). Default 0 |
| 30 | How many samples from before the trigger the capture keeps.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_PRETRIGGER` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | samples, 0-1023 (clamped). Default 0 |
| 31 | Where the capture stands.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_STATE` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no</span> | 0 idle, 1 armed, 2 recording, 3 done |

| 35 | The signal summed per bin. Set it before 34.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_HIST_Y` · Access: set, read · Kept by Save: no</span> | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 3, Iq setpoint |
| 36 | Samples summed since the start. The histogram stops by itself when one bin holds 65535.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_HIST_SAMPLES` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no</span> | samples |
| 39 | The samples per channel a capture holds.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_CAPTURE_LENGTH` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: —</span> | 1024 |

| 93 | The gripper's stroke between positions 0 and 255, from its last calibration ([Gripper mode](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/gripper-mode/#calibrating-the-gripper)). Added in firmware 110.<br><span class="meta">`PARAM_GRIPPER_STROKE` · Access: read only · Kept by Save: no: the gripper calibrates after every power-up</span> | ticks; 0 while the gripper is not calibrated since power-up |

</div>

## What is in force: parameter 79

Parameter 79 says in one read what the drive runs with. `#Info` prints the same at its end, under `In force:`.
Bit 0 is the least significant.

| Bit | Set when |
|---|---|
| 0 | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | an encoder table is measured (in RAM) |
| 2 | the encoder table is in use (parameter 53) |
| 3 | an anti-cogging set is in RAM (harmonics or table) |
| 4 | anti-cogging is on (parameter 37 not 0) |
| 5 | anti-cogging is on as the table (otherwise as the harmonics) |
| 6 | the anti-cogging set in RAM is the one saved in the EEPROM |
| 7 | a current-sense zero trim is applied (parameter 59 or 60 not 0) |
| 8 | the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46) |
| 9 | commutation delay compensation is on (parameter 64 not 0) |
| 10 | the speed estimate is a PLL (parameter 50 is 1 or 2) |
| 11, 12 | 0 on the Spectral Micro (the STEPFOC's fast reading and fast PWM) |
| 13 | sin and cos come from the integer table (parameter 65) |
| 14 | the position input filter is on (parameter 74 not 0) |
| 15 | the velocity-integral deadband is on (parameter 75 not 0) |
| 16-17 | parameter 56 (no effect on the Spectral Micro) |
| 20 | a calibration is running |
| 21 | the encoder table is being measured |
| 22 | the anti-cogging is being identified |
| 23 | the runs after a calibration are about to start |
| 24 | sound is playing ([Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/sound/)) |

Bits 18, 19 and 25 to 31 are 0.

## Reading the capture

A capture records three signals inside the control loop, one sample every *divider* loops, 1024 samples per
channel. It starts when parameter 28 is written: at once (1), when the error flag rises (2, a watchdog trip
included), or when channel A rises (3) or falls (4) through the level of parameter 29. Parameter 30 keeps that many
samples from before the trigger. [Status and diagnostics](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/diagnostics/) shows a whole capture.

1. Set the signals (24, 25, 26), the divider (27), the pre-trigger (30) and, for 3 and 4, the level (29).
2. Write the trigger (28). Parameter 31 reads 1 (armed), 2 (recording), then 3 (done).
3. Read parameter 32 (samples readable) and 33 (the trigger sample's index, −1 if none).
4. Send_Buffer_Read with kind 0, first 0, count = parameter 32: one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per sample, oldest
   first.

The histogram works the same way with parameters 34 to 36 and kind 1: it adds a signal into 256 bins by the
electrical angle or by the encoder, every control loop, until it is stopped or one bin holds 65535 samples.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/sound/ -->

# Sound

Sound through the motor: tones, a queue of timed events and samples, added to the output voltage while the
driver holds or moves. [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/sound/) explains how to use them; parameters 80 to 82 are in the
[parameter table](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/parameters/#sound).

### Send_Sound

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 44</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Sound()`</span></div>

Plays sound through the motor: a tone now, a queue of timed events, or samples. The sound is added to the output voltage, on the q axis by default (parameter 82), and only while the driver holds or moves (position, velocity, current or PD mode); idle or an error stops all of it. Up to 4 tones sound at once (channels 0 to 3), from 20 Hz to below 2500 Hz, half the control-loop rate. Loudness is given as a current: the driver turns it into a voltage with the coil's impedance at that pitch, so low and high notes sound alike. The total voltage is limited to parameter 81 (2000 mV by default; 0 refuses sound). Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer; parameter 80 says what plays. The Python library wraps the operations as Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop.

**8 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Operation | unsigned 8-bit | 0 stop everything (tones, queue, samples); 1 a tone now; 2 add an event to the queue; 3 play the queue; 4 play the samples; 5 samples off, buffer cleared; 6 clear the queue (tones that sound keep sounding) |
| 1 | Channel | unsigned 8-bit | the tone channel, 0-3 (operations 1 and 2) |
| 2-3 | A | unsigned 16-bit | 1, 2: the pitch in Hz (2: 0 silences the channel); 4: the sample rate in Hz, at most the loop rate |
| 4-5 | B | unsigned 16-bit | 1, 2: the loudness in mA; 4: the voltage of a full-scale sample in mV |
| 6-7 | C | unsigned 16-bit | 1: the duration in ms, 0 = until stopped; 2: the wait in ms before the next event, 0 = the next one starts with it |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

The queue holds 31 events and is played by the control loop with loop-exact timing: an event sets one channel's pitch and loudness, then waits. A chord is three events with wait 0 and a fourth with the chord's length. When the queue runs out, every channel falls silent. An event sent to a full queue is dropped. Samples: send them first with Send_Sound_Samples, then operation 4; the driver plays them at the given rate and stops when the buffer runs dry. A frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored. It does not reset the watchdog.

---

### Send_Sound_Samples

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 45</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 to 8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Samples()`</span></div>

Appends 1 to 8 samples (signed 8-bit, one per byte, −127 to 127 = full scale) to the driver's 1024-place sample buffer, which holds 1023 samples. Samples that do not fit are dropped; parameter 80 says how many are buffered. Send_Sound with operation 4 plays them. Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer.

**8 bytes** — eight samples; a shorter frame carries fewer

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Sample 1 | signed 8-bit | the next sample |
| 1 | Sample 2 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 2 | Sample 3 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 3 | Sample 4 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 4 | Sample 5 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 5 | Sample 6 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 6 | Sample 7 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 7 | Sample 8 | signed 8-bit |  |

</div>

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The commands of gripper mode (`#Gripper 1`, saved).

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

**5 bytes**

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA; from firmware 109 its magnitude is used and it stops at 2800 mA; see the gripper manual for the safe range; from firmware 110 the gripper's own limit, the driver's current limit (parameter 16) stays as set |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 idle |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

</div>

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up. From firmware 110 each end is read under a light push and positions 0 and 255 lie a few ticks inside the two ends; this frame sent during a calibration starts it again from its first step. Parameter 93 gives the stroke found.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`. The Python library 1.20 and older combine the two object-detection bits the wrong way round, so their `gripper_object_detection` reads 2 for an object found while closing and 1 for one found while opening; 1.21 and newer read them as the table says.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

<div class="ref-table fields" markdown>

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | the action bit of the last Send_gripper_data_pack (1 after #Grippos); the driver never clears it, so it stays 1 after the move ends: the object detection tells when the move has ended |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit | the driver's temperature error |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit | the driver's watchdog error: the CAN watchdog ran out |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

</div>

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument
type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by
hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/06-operation/uart/) explains the protocol.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored.
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the argument is one word of at most 19 characters, without
  spaces, so a list is written with commas (`#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2`, `#Par 1,200`); firmware 107 and older allowed 20
  characters for name and number together. The line ends with LF (CR before it is
  fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the firmware does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## Every command

## By group

- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/motion/): setpoints and modes, idle and the E-stop (`Estop`, from firmware 110)
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/gains/): the loop gains, the limits, the integrator reset, the current loop bandwidth
- [Calibration and motor parameters](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/calibration/): `Cal` and `Calonly`, the motor's R, L and pole pairs, the constants calibration finds, the calibration settings, the encoder table (`Encal`) and the anti-cogging (`Cogcal`)
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/utility/): save, reset, defaults, identity, errors, temperature, the cyclic output, any parameter (`Par`), the tool id, the watchdog fallback, the product lock
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode
