# SimpleFOC guide

!!! tip "Tested with Simple FOC@^2.3.2 release"

**Main firmware that runs on Spectral micro is [Spectral firmware](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller).**<br />

SimpleFOC is alternative to Spectral Firmware. <br />
The library is intended both for:

* Beginners searching for a simple and user-friendly way to learn how to control BLDC and Stepper motors
* Advanced users ready to dig deeper into the FOC algorithm and optimize the code for their particular application/hardware.

**More info about simple FOC:**

* [Forum](https://community.simplefoc.com/)
* [DOCS](https://docs.simplefoc.com/)
* [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/kWBwuzY32n)
!!! note "SimpleFOC forum and discord is best place to look for help when developing with SimpleFOC library"

## How to install

Follow this [guide](https://docs.simplefoc.com/installation)

!!! warning "This replaces the bootloader"
    This project has no upload offset, so an upload with the programming adapter writes SimpleFOC at
    `0x08000000`, over the bootloader. Firmware updates over UART or CAN stop working. To go back to the Spectral
    firmware, install the bootloader again as in
    [Installing the bootloader on an older board](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/07-firmware/bootloader/), then flash a release.

Your platformio.ini should look like this:

``` ini title="platformio.ini"
[env:genericSTM32F103CB]
platform = ststm32
board = genericSTM32F103CB
framework = arduino
upload_protocol = stlink
build_flags = 
debug_tool = stlink
monitor_speed = 115200
lib_deps = 
	askuric/Simple FOC@^2.3.2
lib_archive = false
```

## SimpleFOC guides
If you want to develop more advanced applications with SimpleFOC you can follow these tutorials:

* [Getting started](https://docs.simplefoc.com/example_from_scratch)
* [Writing the code](https://docs.simplefoc.com/code)
* [SimpleFOC Driver and Support Library](https://github.com/simplefoc/Arduino-FOC-drivers/tree/master)

## Basic example

This example will spin the motor in open loop and enable serial monitor.<br />
Use this code as a base for more advanced code you will develop with SimpleFOC.<br />
The [Spectral-Micro-Simple-FOC](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-Simple-FOC) repository has
this project and more examples in its `examples` folder, among them voltage-torque FOC with the encoder.

``` C++ title="main.cpp"
#include "Arduino.h"
#include "SimpleFOC.h"

// Driver PWM pins
#define PWM_CH1 PA_2
#define PWM_CH2 PA_1 
#define PWM_CH3 PA_0 

// Encoder pins
#define MOSI PB_5
#define MISO PB_4
#define CLK PB_3
#define CSN PA_15

#define SENSE1 PA_4 // Inline current sense
#define SENSE2  PA_3 // Inline current sense

#define TX_COM PB_6
#define RX_COM PB_7

// Current sense resistors
#define SENSE_RESISTOR 0.025f
#define CURRENT_AMP_GAIN 20

// Serial pins
#define Serial Serialx
HardwareSerial Serialx(RX_COM, TX_COM); // PA3, PA2 RX,TX

// BLDC motor & driver instance
// BLDCMotor motor = BLDCMotor(pole pair number, phase resistance (optional) );
BLDCMotor motor = BLDCMotor(11);
//  BLDCDriver3PWM( pin_pwmA, pin_pwmB, pin_pwmC )
BLDCDriver3PWM driver = BLDCDriver3PWM(PWM_CH1, PWM_CH2, PWM_CH3);

//target variable
float target_velocity = 0.1;

void Init_pins();

void setup() {  

  // Init driver enable pins and LED
  Init_pins();

  // pwm frequency to be used [Hz]
  driver.pwm_frequency = 20000;
  // power supply voltage [V]
  driver.voltage_power_supply = 24;
  // Max DC voltage allowed - default voltage_power_supply
  driver.voltage_limit = 5;
  // driver init
  driver.init();
    // link the motor and the driver
  motor.linkDriver(&driver);
  motor.controller = MotionControlType::velocity_openloop;

  // init motor hardware
  motor.init();
    // use monitoring with the BLDCMotor
  Serial.begin(115200);
  Serial.println("Motor ready!");
  _delay(1000);
  // monitoring port
  motor.useMonitoring(Serial);

}

void loop() {
  // open loop velocity movement
  // using motor.voltage_limit and motor.velocity_limit
  motor.move(target_velocity);
  // monitoring function outputting motor variables to the serial terminal 
  motor.monitor();

}

void Init_pins(){
  pinMode(PA_9, OUTPUT);
	pinMode(PA_8, OUTPUT);
	pinMode(PA_10, OUTPUT);
	pinMode(PB_15, OUTPUT);
	pinMode(PB_14, OUTPUT);
	pinMode(PB_13, OUTPUT);

  digitalWrite(PA_9,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PA_8,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PA_10,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_14, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_15, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_13, HIGH);
}
```

# Getting help

- **Questions and discussion**: the [Source Robotics Discord](https://discord.gg/prjUvjmGpZ).
- **A problem with the driver or the firmware**: an issue in the
  [firmware repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller/issues); see
  [Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/support/report-a-problem/) for what to include.
- **A mistake on a page of this site**: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see
  [Contributing](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/support/contributing/).
- **Orders and hardware**: [source-robotics.com](https://source-robotics.com/).

Before you ask, [Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/08-troubleshooting/) goes through the common symptoms, and `#Info` tells
most of what anyone will ask you for.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/support/report-a-problem/ -->

# Report a problem

Open an issue in the [firmware repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller/issues)
for the driver and its firmware, or in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/issues)
for the Python library. Include:

1. **The output of `#Info`, `#Error` and `#Param`**, copied from the terminal. They carry the hardware and
   firmware version, the motor parameters, the calibration state, the errors and the gains.
2. **The motor**: type, and the resistance, inductance and pole pairs calibration found (`#Info` prints them).
3. **The supply**: voltage, and whether it has a current limit.
4. **What you did and what happened**: the commands, in order, and the driver's answers; the calibration log if it
   is about calibration.
5. **How it is wired**: a photo of the board on the motor and of the cables helps more than a description.

For a problem with this documentation, the *Report it* link at the end of the page opens an issue in the
documentation repository with the page already named.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/110/support/contributing/ -->

# Contributing

This documentation lives in [Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-docs](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-docs). A
small fix can be made from the browser: the *Edit it on GitHub* link at the end of every page opens the page's
source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

## How the site is built

- The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's `README.md` says how to
  preview it locally.
- The site describes one firmware release, named in `versions.yml`. The command IDs, frame lengths, the UART
  command list and the defaults in the Reference are read from the firmware's source at that release's tag by
  `tools/sync_firmware.py`; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the commands are in
  `docs/includes/can_commands.yml` and `uart_commands.yml`.
- Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to `main` publishes the
  site under its firmware version with [mike](https://github.com/jimporter/mike).

## House rules

- Facts come from the firmware. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware is right; fix the page, or
  report the firmware.
- Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
- Write for someone who has the driver in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order, then
  why.
- Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
- Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.
